title: 996: China's Brutal 72-Hour Work Week #shorts
description:
9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week. How 996 became normal in Chinese tech, the 996.ICU protest, and the 2021 ruling that called it illegal.

New China Short every day; full reality-show recap every Saturday. Subscribe to @mainlandunpacked.

Sources: Supreme People's Court & Ministry of Human Resources typical cases (Aug 2021); PRC Labor Law Art. 41. Footage: China News Service; Videos library (CC BY).

scenes.text: Nine a.m. to nine p.m., six days a week. In China, it has a name.
China's own labor law caps it at about forty-eight: forty regular hours, plus up to thirty-six hours of overtime a month.
In 2019, tech workers fought back online with a GitHub project called 996.ICU: work 996, end up in the ICU.
scenes.say: In 2019, tech workers fought back online with a GitHub project called nine nine six dot I C U. Work nine nine six, end up in the I C U.
scenes.label: Zhongguancun, Beijing's tech hub

scenes.text: The same year, Alibaba founder Jack Ma called working 996 a huge blessing.
scenes.say: The same year, Alibaba founder Jack Ma called working nine nine six a huge blessing.

scenes.text: In 2021, China's top court and labor ministry declared it illegal, after a courier firm fired a worker for refusing 996.
scenes.say: In 2021, China's top court and labor ministry declared it illegal, after a courier firm fired a worker for refusing nine nine six.

scenes.text: But many workers say the long hours never went away. Would you work 996 for double pay?
